title: Berghuis v. Thompkins (2010)
key_points: Holding: Federally, a suspect must invoke the right to silence unambiguously; remaining mostly silent is not an invocation.
New Jersey: NJ courts require officers to scrupulously honor any indication, even ambiguous, that a suspect wishes to stop; clarify before continuing.
officer_notes: Scenario: A suspect sits silent for most of a long interview, then answers one question.
Takeaway: NJ is more protective; treat ambiguous statements as a cue to stop and clarify.
